fields.meta_title: Project Request Form Builder With Routing Rules | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a project request form that sends each request to the person who approves it and ranks new work before anyone commits hours to it.
fields.h1: Build a Project Request Form Your Intake Team Can Act On
fields.hero_description: Describe how your team decides on new work. Emergent builds the project request form and routes each request to its approver, saving every one in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Blank Request Form Leaves Undecided
fields.features_subheading: A PDF collects the idea. Who reviews it, which budget pays for it and when the work could start are still settled in someone's inbox.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that fit the request type

Show each request type its own fields. An IT request asks which systems the project touches, while a facilities request asks for the building and for photos of the leak or damage.
fields.feature_2:
Sign-off before your team sees it

Send a request to its sponsor or data owner before it reaches your intake meeting. The sign-off is recorded with a name and a time, and the request then moves on to the next step.
fields.feature_3:
Routing by estimated cost

Route each request by its estimate. Work under your line becomes a work order, larger jobs go to the budget committee, and the requester can see which path the request has taken.
fields.feature_4:
Rush flags on short deadlines

Compare the requested due date with the lead time your team needs. A deadline that is too short is marked rush and waits for a manager to approve it, instead of jumping the queue.
fields.feature_5:
Ranking against team hours

Score each request on the criteria your board picked, then rank it against this quarter's team hours. The board sees which requests fit now and which ones wait for the next round.
fields.feature_6:
Your intake app, in your repo

Export the full code to your GitHub on paid plans whenever you want. Your routing rules and every past request then live in a codebase your team controls and can extend later.

fields.why_description: A PDF request form records what someone wants. It cannot tell them who approves it or when the work could start.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Intake Desks and the Rules They Run
fields.tab_content_1:
Registrar sign-off comes before IT sees the request

Westbrook College's IT office runs every new project through one form. Admissions wants campus tour sign-ups to create applicant records. The form asks which systems the work touches, and the answer includes the student records system. Registrar Dana Ortiz signs off first, before IT's Thursday intake meeting.
fields.tab_content_2:
Capital planning gets any estimate over $50,000

Lakeview County's parks department needs a new roof on the Elm Street community center. The request carries photos of the leak and an $84,000 contractor estimate. Facilities turns anything under $50,000 into a work order. This one is over the line and goes to the capital planning committee.
fields.tab_content_3:
Rush review for signage due in 9 business days

Northwind Outfitters' brand studio needs 15 business days to produce in-store signage. The retail team asks for window posters for a weekend sale that opens in 9 business days. The form counts the days as the date is picked and marks the request rush. Creative director Marcus Bell approves it or offers a later date.
fields.tab_content_4:
The quarter's 1,200 hours go to the top four requests

Globex Health's project office scores every request out of 25 for value, urgency and effort. Requests are funded in score order until the quarter's 1,200 team hours run out. Four requests fit in 1,150 hours. The patient portal redesign scored 17 of 25 and needs 300 hours. It waits for next quarter.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Project Request Form
fields.howto_description: Start from the decisions your team already makes about new work. The form should ask for exactly what those decisions need.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Name the person who says yes
fields.howto_step_1_des: Gather the last 20 requests your team received, wherever they arrived, by email or in a hallway conversation. Note what you had to ask each requester afterward. Those follow-up questions are the fields your current form is missing.
fields.howto_step_2_des: For each kind of request, write down who approves it, such as a data owner or a budget holder. When a request needs two approvals, put them in order, and let the second approver read the first one's note before deciding.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Turn habits into thresholds the form can apply. Estimates over $50,000 go to capital planning, and deadlines under 15 business days are rush. Words like large or urgent get argued over in every meeting, while a number settles it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: If more requests arrive than your team can take on, agree on a score before the form goes live. Weigh the value of each request against the effort it needs, and the review board gets a ranked list it can defend.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your fields and rules into one prompt. Emergent builds the request form, with a database that holds every request and the routing between approvers. When a rule changes later, describe the new rule in a sentence.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Give each requester a status page, plus an email whenever the request changes step or someone leaves a note. Requesters who can check the status for themselves stop writing to the intake inbox to ask where things stand.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Send a few old requests through it
fields.howto_step_7_des: Re-enter five of the requests from step 1 and check where each one lands. Every request should reach the approver you would have picked by hand. Fix any rule that sends one elsewhere before you share the form.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is two university project request PDFs (Coppin State IT, Oklahoma facilities), a SharePoint list, a WeWeb app template, a Jotform template, a 2018 Nutrient blog post, a Pinterest board and Workzone's intake software tour. Google's AI Overview lists the sections a request should hold, and the related searches add PDFs and construction. Every result stops at the blank form. None shows what the office receiving requests does with them: send a request to the person who must sign off first, divert large jobs to a different budget, flag a deadline the team cannot meet, and fund requests in order until the quarter's hours run out. This page defines the form, then shows four intake offices doing exactly that, with each rule visible on the form.
